description:
List forms
Returns the forms visible to the current identity (`kind=form`, excluding tables and quick payment forms). A personal token returns the forms the user created and those shared with them; an account token returns every form in the account.
By default sorted by id descending (that is, by creation time descending), and `next` is the id of the first row of the next page; when `sort` is passed, rows are sorted by the given field and `next` becomes `row:<offset>`.
50 per page by default, adjustable with `limit` (max 1000).
- Each row carries `entries_count` (entry count) and `last_entry_created_at` (when the last entry was received), usable with `filters` / `sort`.
- With `include_transactions=true`, forms bound to a payment account carry `transactions` payment statistics.
Returns schema "FormListResponse" (see get_schema).
Usually the first call of a session: get the form token here, then call get_form / list_entries.
name: list_forms
title: List forms

q.description: Fuzzy match on name (case-insensitive; matches both the public name and the in-product name). Accepts several values (`q[]=A&q[]=B`), matching forms whose name contains any of them. Equivalent to `filters=[{"field":"form_name","operator":"like","value":...}]`.

items.description: One filter condition. A `filters` parameter is the JSON text of an array of these, combined with AND; each endpoint says which fields and operators it takes.

field.description: What to filter on; a field api_code for entries, where `creator_id` (`eq` with a user id, at most once) and `serial_number` (`eq` / `any_in` / `none_in`, several intersected) also work, or a form attribute such as `created_at` for form lists. Required unless the deprecated `api_code` or `trigger` is given instead.

operator.description: Comparison; `equal` / `not_equal` / `start` / `end` are aliases of `eq` / `ne` / `gte` / `lte`. Each field type accepts only some operators, and an unsupported one returns 400 listing the available ones.

value.description: Condition value; its type depends on the field and the operator: a two-element array `[min, max]` for `between` / `not_between` (`{"<column api_code>": [min, max]}` on a matrix or table field), `{"unit": "day", "n": 30}` for `within_last` (unit minute / day / week / month), no value for `null` / `not_null`, a choice api_code or label on a choice field (a cascading drop-down also takes a `level1-level2` path), and serial numbers of the related table for `any_in` / `none_in` on a relation field.

filters.description:
Filters, an array of ScopeCondition objects; conditions are combined with AND. Filterable fields and operators:
| field | type | operators |
|---|---|---|
| `form_name` | text | `eq` `ne` `any_in` `none_in` `like` `not_like` |
| `created_at` | time | `eq` `ne` `gte` `gt` `lte` `lt` `within_last` |
| `last_entry_created_at` | time | same as above (forms that have never received an entry have no value) |
| `entries_count` | integer | `eq` `ne` `gte` `gt` `lte` `lt` |

The value of `within_last` looks like `{"unit":"day","n":30}` (unit can be minute / day / week / month), meaning the window going back from now.
Example: `[{"field":"last_entry_created_at","operator":"within_last","value":{"unit":"day","n":7}}]`

sort.description:
Sort rules, an array of FormSortRule objects, applied in order.
Sortable fields: `created_at`, `last_entry_created_at`, `entries_count`; any other field, an invalid order or unparseable JSON returns 400.
With `sort`, `next` becomes a cursor of the form `row:<offset>`, usable only in requests with the same `sort`; rows with equal values may change order between pages.

next.description: `next` from the previous page's response, passed back as is to get the next page. Cannot be combined with `page` or `skip`.

page.description: Page number from 1, for jumping to a page or reading pages in parallel; `(page - 1) × limit` can be at most 10000, and the returned `next` continues from there. Cannot be combined with `next` or `skip`.

skip.description: Deprecated, use `page`. Starting row offset (from 0, at most 10000); the returned `next` still pages onward. Cannot be combined with `next` or `page`.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 50, max 1000 (larger values are treated as 1000). With 0, returns only `total`, and `data` is empty.

include_transactions.description: When `true`, forms bound to a payment account (merchant account / WeChat Pay / Alipay) carry `transactions` payment statistics; unbound forms have no such key. Not included by default.

Check whether fields already hold data
Use before deleting a field or choice: checks in batch whether fields (or single choices of a field) already have submitted entries. Deleting a field or choice that still has entries deletes those entries with it, and they cannot be recovered.

description:
List entries
Returns form entries page by page, 50 per page by default, set with `limit` (max 1000). Sorted by serial number ascending by default; `next` is the serial number of the first entry of the next page.
- `filters` / `keyword` trigger a conditional query; `created_at` returns only entries created at or after that time (and sorts by creation time instead);
  in both these cases, and when `sort` is passed, `next` becomes a row offset.
- `fields` returns only the given fields (the serial number is always returned).
- Each entry is keyed by field api_code (a field with api_code_alias set is keyed by its alias); for the value shapes see `EntryData`.

title: List entries

form_token.description: Form token (`token` from `GET /forms`); a 24-character hexadecimal form id is also accepted.

fields.description: Return only these fields. A JSON array, a comma-separated string or a repeated parameter, of field api_codes; the serial number is always returned. Returns 400 listing the available fields when an api_code is unknown.

items.description: One filter condition. A `filters` parameter is the JSON text of an array of these, combined with AND; each endpoint says which fields and operators it takes.

field.description: What to filter on; a field api_code for entries, where `creator_id` (`eq` with a user id, at most once) and `serial_number` (`eq` / `any_in` / `none_in`, several intersected) also work, or a form attribute such as `created_at` for form lists. Required unless the deprecated `api_code` or `trigger` is given instead.

operator.description: Comparison; `equal` / `not_equal` / `start` / `end` are aliases of `eq` / `ne` / `gte` / `lte`. Each field type accepts only some operators, and an unsupported one returns 400 listing the available ones.

value.description: Condition value; its type depends on the field and the operator: a two-element array `[min, max]` for `between` / `not_between` (`{"<column api_code>": [min, max]}` on a matrix or table field), `{"unit": "day", "n": 30}` for `within_last` (unit minute / day / week / month), no value for `null` / `not_null`, a choice api_code or label on a choice field (a cascading drop-down also takes a `level1-level2` path), and serial numbers of the related table for `any_in` / `none_in` on a relation field.

filters.description:
Filters, an array of ScopeCondition objects; conditions are combined with AND. Besides field api_codes, `creator_id` and `serial_number` can be filtered on.
- To find entries whose multiple-choice field contains a choice, use `any_in` (`none_in` to exclude); `eq` is not "contains": it matches only entries with exactly the same set of choices.

keyword.description: Full-text keyword (at most 200 characters), fuzzy-matched across all searchable fields. Forms with more than 99999 entries and no analytics engine enabled do not support full-text search (returns 400), unless `creator_id` also restricts the submitter.

api_code.description: api_code of the field to sort by; only sortable fields are allowed

sort.description:
Sort rules, an array of SortRule objects, applied in order, with ascending serial number appended automatically at the end.
Only sortable fields are allowed; otherwise returns 400 listing the sortable fields. With `sort`, `next` becomes a row offset. Without it, entries come by serial number, or by creation time when `filters` has a `created_at` condition.

next.description: `next` from the previous page's response. Under the default sort it is a serial-number cursor (returns entries with serial number ≥ this value); with filters / creation-time ordering / an explicit sort it is a row offset. Cannot be combined with `page` or `skip`. Also accepts a string: one starting with an integer is read as that integer, anything else as 0, i.e. starting from the first page.

page.description: Page number from 1, for jumping to a page or reading pages in parallel; `(page - 1) × limit` can be at most 10000, and the returned `next` continues from there. Cannot be combined with `next` or `skip`.

skip.description: Deprecated, use `page`. Starting row offset (from 0, max 10000). Cannot be combined with `next` or `page`.

description:
Create an entry
Submits one entry keyed by field api_code (or api_code_alias). Unknown keys are ignored; when no valid key remains, returns 400, with `error_description` starting with `Entry attributes cannot be empty` and naming each dropped key (not a field of this form, or a signature / calculated field that cannot be written).
- The form's field display rules and field validation still apply; a validation failure returns 400, and `error_description` is `{ "<api_code>": ["error"] }` serialized as a JSON string.
- Mobile fields skip SMS verification; signature fields and calculated fields cannot be written.
- Returns 403 when the form's entry count has reached the plan limit.
- Attachment fields accept several forms of input; see `EntryInput`.
Returns schema "Entry" (see get_schema).
name: create_entry
title: Create an entry

form_token.description: Form token (`token` from `GET /forms`); a 24-character hexadecimal form id is also accepted.

entry.description:
Field values for writing an entry, keyed by field api_code or api_code_alias. Unknown keys and non-writable fields (signature, formula) are ignored.
Choice fields take the choice api_code or the choice label; see the table below for cascading drop-downs and choice extra text. Number fields accept a number or a numeric string.

| Field | How to write |
|---|---|
| Single-line / multi-line text, name, mobile, email, phone, website, ID card | String |
| Single choice, drop-down | `"choice api_code"` or `"choice label"`; extra text via `"<api_code>_extended_text": {"<choice>": "extra text"}`, "Other" text via `"<api_code>_other": "..."` |
| Multiple choice | Array, items as above |
| Image single choice / image multiple choice | Choice api_code (string / array) |
| Cascading drop-down | `{"level_1": "...", "level_2": "..."}` (api_code or label) |
| Number, rating, NPS | Number |
| Yes/No | Boolean |
| Date | `"2012-12-25"` or `"2012-12-25 12:13:15"` (Beijing time, UTC+8) |
| Time | `{"hour": "12", "minute": "15"}` |
| Address | `{"province","city","district","street"}` |
| Geolocation | `{"longitude","latitude","address"}` |
| File upload (multiple allowed) | Array; each item is one of: the id of an uploaded attachment; the download URL of an attachment already on this form (to keep it); `{"base64": "...", "file_name": "a.png", "content_type": "image/png"}` (≤ 5MB; `base64` may also be a data URI) |
| Goods | `[{"value": "goods item api_code", "number": 2, "specification": {"spec dimension": "option"}?}]` |
| Matrix fill-in / matrix scale | `{"<statement api_code>": {"<column api_code>": value}}` |
| Matrix single choice | `{"<statement api_code>": "choice api_code"}` |
| Table | `[{"<column api_code>": value}, ...]`; attachment columns are written like file upload |
| Inline blanks | `{"<sub-field api_code>": "..."}` |
| Ranking | Ordered array `["choice api_code", ...]` |
| Form association | token / id of the associated entry, or a display value matched by the association key (an array for multiple association keys) |
| Reservation | `[{"api_code": "item", "scheduled_at": "2021-04-26", "end_at"?: "...", "number": 1}]` |
| Color mark | `"color_mark": "<color api_code or name>"` |
| International mobile number | Also pass `"<api_code>_country_id"` / `"<api_code>_country_code"` |

description:
Create a view on a form
Creates a new view on the form, created by the caller; visibility defaults to cooperators when not passed, and position is the highest position among the currently visible views plus 1. Each user can have at most 100 views on one form; at the limit, returns 422 (View limit reached). When view_type is kanban and kanban_group_by_api_code is not passed, the server picks the grouping field; when kanban_hidden_groups is not passed, the __unset__ group is hidden by default; when prefer_columns is empty, the form's default columns are used (at most 5 columns for a kanban view, serial_number included). Returns 422 when filter is invalid (not an array, unknown field, unsupported operator, invalid value). Returns 422 when model validation fails (e.g. name is empty or longer than 120 characters, or the grouping field does not support kanban grouping). Form views (view_type form): supported only on tables, otherwise 422; title defaults to the table name; without field_overrides, all fillable columns are selected in the current column order; published defaults to false (the fill link does not work while unpublished). title / description / published / field_overrides apply only to form views; using them on another type returns 422. Creating, updating or deleting a form view (including switching a view to or from a form view) requires the caller to hold a predefined role on the table that can add entries, otherwise 403; an account token is exempt. Returns 422 when a fill item's column does not exist, cannot be a fill item, or sets a validation its column type does not support; the error message names the column's api_code.

Filters, an array of ScopeCondition objects; conditions are combined with AND. Filterable fields and operators:
| field | type | operators |
|---|---|---|
| `form_name` | text | `eq` `ne` `any_in` `none_in` `like` `not_like` |
| `created_at` | time | `eq` `ne` `gte` `gt` `lte` `lt` `within_last` |
| `last_entry_created_at` | time | same as above (forms that have never received an entry have no value) |
| `entries_count` | integer | `eq` `ne` `gte` `gt` `lte` `lt` |

The value of `within_last` looks like `{"unit":"day","n":30}` (unit can be minute / day / week / month), meaning the window going back from now.
Example: `[{"field":"last_entry_created_at","operator":"within_last","value":{"unit":"day","n":7}}]`

description:
Counts the entries matching the conditions, without returning them. A single form_token counts one form (keyword / filters supported); an array of up to 10 tokens counts several forms in one call and gives the total (filters can then use only created_at / updated_at / creator_id, and keyword is not supported).
Several forms (form_token is an array): Counts, in one call, the entries matching the filters in each of up to 10 forms / tables, plus their total.
- A token that cannot be accessed (does not exist, or does not belong to the caller) does not fail the whole request; its row returns `unavailable` with the reason instead. The total adds up only the rows that could be counted.
- Field api_codes mean different things in each form, so `filters` can use only the three form-independent conditions `created_at` / `updated_at` / `creator_id`; any other field returns 400.
- `keyword` is not supported (passing it returns 400); to search several forms by keyword, use `GET /entries/search`.
name: count_entries
title: Count entries

form_token.description: A form token, or an array of up to 10 tokens to count several forms in one call

items.description: One filter condition. A `filters` parameter is the JSON text of an array of these, combined with AND; each endpoint says which fields and operators it takes.

field.description: What to filter on; a field api_code for entries, where `creator_id` (`eq` with a user id, at most once) and `serial_number` (`eq` / `any_in` / `none_in`, several intersected) also work, or a form attribute such as `created_at` for form lists. Required unless the deprecated `api_code` or `trigger` is given instead.

operator.description: Comparison; `equal` / `not_equal` / `start` / `end` are aliases of `eq` / `ne` / `gte` / `lte`. Each field type accepts only some operators, and an unsupported one returns 400 listing the available ones.

value.description: Condition value; its type depends on the field and the operator: a two-element array `[min, max]` for `between` / `not_between` (`{"<column api_code>": [min, max]}` on a matrix or table field), `{"unit": "day", "n": 30}` for `within_last` (unit minute / day / week / month), no value for `null` / `not_null`, a choice api_code or label on a choice field (a cascading drop-down also takes a `level1-level2` path), and serial numbers of the related table for `any_in` / `none_in` on a relation field.

filters.description:
Filters, an array of ScopeCondition objects; conditions are combined with AND. Besides field api_codes, `creator_id` and `serial_number` can be filtered on.
- To find entries whose multiple-choice field contains a choice, use `any_in` (`none_in` to exclude); `eq` is not "contains": it matches only entries with exactly the same set of choices.

keyword.description: Full-text keyword (at most 200 characters), fuzzy-matched across all searchable fields. Forms with more than 99999 entries and no analytics engine enabled do not support full-text search (returns 400), unless `creator_id` also restricts the submitter.

matched_entries.description: Number of entries matching the conditions
